text:
**My pick is the Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with a 200W panel.** It's $699 (list $879) on Amazon, with a 4.5-star rating across about 1,400 reviews. It has a 1,070Wh LiFePO4 battery and 1,500W AC output. Amazon also tags it as an "Overall Pick." A roundup at Talk of the House also names it Editor's Choice, citing its balance of power, portability (23.8 lbs) and fast charging, though that site is a review roundup that earns affiliate commissions.
[Amazon listing](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included) · [Review roundup](https://www.talkofthehouse.com/best-solar-generator-kits-with-panels/)

**Other good options, depending on your needs:**

| Tighter budget | UDPOWER S1200 + 120W panel (1,190Wh) | $549.99, 4.1★ (only 41 reviews) | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included) |

**Things to know before buying:**
- **Check what ships in the box.** The Talk of the House review says some kits' panels ship separately from the power station, so confirm the panel is included on the product page.
- **Solar charging is slow.** The Jackery review estimates 6 to 8 hours in full sun for a 200W panel on the 1000 v2, and longer when it's cloudy. More panels charge faster.
- **Size it to what you'll run.** The 1,000Wh class covers camping, CPAP use and short outages. For a fridge over a multi-day outage, go to 2,000Wh or more.
- **Costco is an option if you're a member.** It lists the Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 with a solar panel at $899.99, but it was out of stock at the Mountain View warehouse in the snapshot. [Costco](https://www.costco.com/home-solar-power.html)
- **Prices come from search snapshots.** Amazon prices and coupons change often, so confirm at checkout.

If you tell me what you want to power (camping, home outages, RV) and your budget, I can narrow it down to one.
